healthcareSystem: Government healthcare for citizens; tourists and expatriates use private hospitals. Good-quality facilities in Kuwait City.
qualityNotes: Good healthcare in Kuwait City with modern private hospitals. Public hospitals are available but can be overcrowded. English is widely spoken in medical settings. Limited facilities outside Kuwait City.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-12am. Some 24/7 options in hospitals and malls. Closed during Friday prayer.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked. Pharmacists speak English and Arabic. Kuwait has strict drug control laws. Verify medications are legal before bringing them.
prescriptionRules: Kuwait has strict drug control laws. Many common medications are restricted or banned. Prescription required for most medications. Foreign prescriptions not accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Zero tolerance. Severe criminal penalties including imprisonment.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Requires documentation and advance approval from Kuwait Ministry of Health.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English and Arabic listing all medications. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, obtain prior approval from Kuwait's Ministry of Health. Drug law violations carry severe penalties.

travelInsurance.tips: Private healthcare is expensive. ER visits cost $200+. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage recommended. Public hospitals may treat emergencies but expect long wait times.

required: Yellow Fever (if arriving from endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers.

waterNotes: Tap water is desalinated and safe to drink. Bottled water widely available and preferred by most.
foodSafetyTips: Good food safety standards in restaurants. Be cautious in extreme summer heat. Excellent Middle Eastern cuisine available at reputable establishments.
medicalTourismNote: Kuwait is not a major medical tourism destination. Kuwaitis often travel to the UK, US, or Germany for specialized treatment.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Kuwait. Emergency number 112, strict drug laws, banned medications, pharmacy tips, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Dar Al Shifa Hospital
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Kuwait City (Hawally, near The Avenues Mall)
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital. Modern facilities. International patient services.

hospitals.name: Al Salam International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Established private hospital with 24/7 emergency department.

hospitals.name: Mubarak Al-Kabeer Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major public teaching hospital. Largest emergency department in Kuwait.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care in Kuwait City with modern private clinics.
dentalCare.costRange: KWD 15-40 ($49-131) for consultation; KWD 30-100 ($98-327) for procedures
dentalCare.notes: Many internationally trained dentists. Quality is good at private clinics.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. Private dental clinics available on weekdays.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: Contact Kuwait Psychological Association or hospital psychiatric departments
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available at private hospitals and clinics in Kuwait City.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services developing. Private hospitals offer psychiatric consultations.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is improving in newer buildings. Shopping malls and modern hotels are accessible. Older areas have limited accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Limited accessible public transport. Taxis and ride-hailing available.
accessibilityInfo.tips: The Avenues Mall and newer attractions are accessible. Kuwait Towers area has some accessible pathways.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements.
covidStatus.notes: Heat-related illness is the primary health concern. Summer temperatures often exceed 50°C (122°F).

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals require upfront payment or insurance authorization. Keep all receipts and medical reports. English documentation available at most facilities.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower (or free for residents). Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Local hospitals handle routine cases; for complex care that exceeds local capacity, regional referral options are well-established. Dubai is the regional referral hub for North Africa and South Asia, and Gulf-state tertiary hospitals (Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Hamad Medical Corporation, Sheba Medical Center in Israel) are well-equipped.
